items.title: [arxiv.org] Supervised clinical AI trial records no safety stops; separate study finds better visit preparation
items.content_html:
A supervised urgent-care trial of conversational AI recorded no safety stops, while a separate randomized study found that a structured chatbot improved patients’ preparation for appointments. In the urgent-care trial, researchers at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center tested Google’s AMIE system with 114 patients; 98 completed both the chat and physician visit, with doctors monitoring chats live. The study assessed feasibility, not whether AI improved health outcomes.

The randomized study, posted as a preprint on arXiv, involved 802 U.S. adults and found higher clinician-rated preparation and patient-reported readiness with a structured visit-preparation agent than with a minimally prompted chatbot. The AMIE findings apply to physician-supervised chats, while the randomized study calls for further research on communication during visits and clinical outcomes.

items.title: [cw39.com] Researchers favor permanent standard time as US debates clock changes
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Most U.S. clocks turn back one hour Nov. 1, as new research reviews renew debate over whether year-round standard time or daylight saving time better supports health. A Canadian policy analysis and a review focused on people with mental illness argue that permanent standard time better protects sleep, mood and biological rhythms. A broader review of population studies, however, finds a mix of harms and benefits from seasonal clock changes and summer daylight saving time. Permanent daylight saving time would delay winter sunrise, while permanent standard time would bring earlier summer sunrises and winter sunsets. The U.S. House passed a bill to make daylight saving time permanent in July 2026, but the Senate has not taken it up. The next seasonal clock change is scheduled for March 14, 2027.

items.content_html:
🎨 🔭 ✏️

Scientists believe the discovery could pave the way for earlier intervention and future treatments designed to prevent Alzheimer’s before memory problems begin.
